headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Khoj’s shared indexed notes feeding PaddleOCR’s document parsing; no documented isolation between the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and supports shared index across clients, so attacker-controlled content in its corpus can reach outputs. PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can be used on content from Khoj, creating a plausible bridge where parsed text is treated as trusted input. No explicit provenance or isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is fed into Khoj without provenance tagging, injection risk exists.
IF both agents operate on the same document corpus, attacker-controlled text can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all PaddleOCR outputs before ingestion.
Restrict Khoj to read-only retrieval from a quarantined index.
Manually inspect OCR output for instruction-like text before reuse.
Separate corpora so untrusted documents are not indexed by Khoj.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents and has broad network egress; PaddleOCR processes documents and images with allowlisted egress. If the same sensitive files are routed through both, data can leave the local workspace through either agent’s API calls. The profiles do not show hard isolation, so the shared-document pathway is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are sent to PaddleOCR for OCR, their contents may be exposed through networked processing.
IF Khoj indexes the same sensitive files, those contents can be surfaced in downstream outputs.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared OCR pipeline.
Use a local-only OCR deployment for private documents.
Disable external search/providers for the Khoj workspace handling secrets.
Review and redact documents before indexing or OCR.
requires-engineering: enforce per-document data-class routing and egress controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read the filesystem but cannot write it, modify git, or spawn subprocesses; PaddleOCR exposes browser and allowlisted network egress but no filesystem write. That means direct write-write conflict is absent, and the main overlap is read/processing of shared documents. This is a limited conflict surface, not a dangerous mutable-resource collision.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access not shown in the profiles, conflict severity would rise.
IF shared mutable resources are added later, concurrent updates could collide.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared inputs.
Avoid giving either agent git or filesystem write permissions.
Run them in separate workspaces.
Serialize any manual handoff steps.
requires-engineering: add locking if mutable shared resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can generate retrieval-based answers from indexed notes, and PaddleOCR can turn documents into text that Khoj may then treat as authoritative. Because no verification step is documented between OCR output and downstream use, errors or hallucinated text can cascade into user-facing answers or actions. The pair creates a default pipeline where one agent’s output becomes the other’s input.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is ingested into Khoj without human review, OCR errors can propagate.
IF Khoj answers are used as source text for later document processing, mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between OCR and retrieval.
Mark OCR text as untrusted in downstream prompts.
Compare OCR output against the source document for critical fields.
Limit automated actions based on Khoj answers.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare conflicting residency, certification, or retention constraints. Khoj handles personal notes and indexed documents, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images, but the profiles do not show a specific compliance mismatch such as PHI, EU-only data, or divergent retention policies. With no documented mismatch, only a low residual compliance concern remains.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through a non-compliant deployment, compliance risk increases.
IF retention settings differ between the two deployments, deletion/export obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Confirm both deployments’ retention settings.
Keep regulated data out of the pair unless policies are aligned.
Document data residency for each service.
Review logs for sensitive content.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data.
